source: Toprank Review Academy (TRA) Nursing Module – Complete Handout

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client with a prosthetic heart valve is scheduled for tooth extraction. The nurse anticipates:
questions.rationale: High-risk clients receive antibiotic prophylaxis before dental procedures to prevent endocarditis.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Endocarditis Prevention (PDF p. 312)
questions.quote: Antibiotic prophylaxis is recommended for high-risk patients

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client going home on IV antibiotics for endocarditis should be taught to:
questions.rationale: Record temperature daily for up to 6 weeks, keep aseptic IV technique, and report fever.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Endocarditis Home Care (PDF p. 312)
questions.quote: Instruct the client to record the temperature daily for up to 6 weeks and report fever.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which is the most common type of myocarditis?
questions.rationale: Viral myocarditis is most common.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Myocarditis (PDF p. 312)
questions.quote: Viral myocarditis is the most common type

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Clients with myocarditis require close monitoring when given digoxin because they:
questions.rationale: Myocarditis increases sensitivity to digitalis; watch for dysrhythmias, nausea, vomiting.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Myocarditis Nursing Alert (PDF p. 312)
questions.quote: Patients with myocarditis are sensitive to digitalis.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Pericarditis chest pain is typically relieved by:
questions.rationale: Pain worsens with breathing or lying flat and is relieved by sitting and leaning forward.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Pericarditis (PDF p. 313)
questions.quote: relieved with a forward leaning or sitting position

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which is the most characteristic sign of pericarditis?
questions.rationale: A creaky, scratchy friction rub at the left sternal border is diagnostic.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Pericarditis (PDF p. 313)
questions.quote: A pericardial friction rub is diagnostic feature of pericarditis.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Before pericardiocentesis, the head of the bed is elevated to:
questions.rationale: HOB at 45–60 degrees brings the heart close to the chest wall for needle insertion.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Pericardiocentesis (PDF p. 313)
questions.quote: The head of the bed is elevated to 45 to 60 degrees

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which finding indicates successful pericardiocentesis?
questions.rationale: Expected: decreased CVP, increased BP, loss of pulsus paradoxus, flatter neck veins.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Pericardiocentesis (PDF p. 313)
questions.quote: Decrease in central venous pressure

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Beck's triad of cardiac tamponade includes:
options: Chest pain, ST elevation, Q waves
questions.rationale: Beck's triad: jugular vein distention, hypotension, distant heart sounds.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Cardiac Tamponade (PDF p. 314)
questions.quote: BECK's Triad

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Pulsus paradoxus is a systolic BP drop during inspiration of more than:
questions.rationale: Pulsus paradoxus: >10 mm Hg drop during inspiration, seen in tamponade.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Cardiac Tamponade (PDF p. 314)
questions.quote: >10 mm Hg drop in blood pressure during inspiration

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Chest pain on exertion, relieved by rest and nitroglycerin in a predictable pattern, is:
questions.rationale: Stable angina is predictable, exertional, and relieved by rest or nitroglycerin.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Types of Angina (PDF p. 314)
questions.quote: Stable angina: predictable and consistent pain that occurs on exertion

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Chest pain at rest with transient ST elevation from coronary vasospasm is:
questions.rationale: Variant (Prinzmetal's) angina is caused by vasospasm; calcium channel blockers are used.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Types of Angina (PDF p. 314)
questions.quote: caused by coronary artery vasospasm

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which activity may trigger angina and should be avoided?
questions.rationale: Heavy meals, cold, exertion, and stress trigger angina.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Angina Triggers (PDF p. 315)
questions.quote: Eating a heavy meal

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Nitroglycerin relieves angina mainly by:
questions.rationale: Venous pooling decreases blood returning to the heart, reducing workload.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Nitroglycerin (PDF p. 315)
questions.quote: Nitroglycerine causes dilation of the veins

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which calcium channel blocker is used primarily for coronary vasospasm?
questions.rationale: Diltiazem is used for vasospasm; metoprolol is a beta-blocker.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Angina Medications (PDF p. 316)
questions.quote: Diltiazem (Cardizem, Tiazac) used primary treatment for vasospasm

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which feature distinguishes MI pain from angina?
questions.rationale: MI pain lasts longer than 30 minutes and is relieved only by opioids.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, MI Assessment (PDF p. 316)
questions.quote: The pain associated with an MI usually lasts longer than 30 minutes

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which cardiac marker rises first after myocardial infarction?
questions.rationale: Myoglobin rises within 1–3 hours, earliest but not cardiac-specific.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Cardiac Enzymes (PDF p. 317)
questions.quote: First enzyme to elevate due to decreased oxygenation

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which ECG change indicates acute myocardial injury?
questions.rationale: MI ECG: ST elevation, T-wave inversion, abnormal Q waves.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, MI ECG (PDF p. 316)
questions.quote: ST-segment elevation

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Thrombolytic therapy in acute MI aims to:
questions.rationale: Thrombolytics lyse the thrombus, restoring flow and limiting damage.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, MI Pharmacologic Therapy (PDF p. 317)
questions.quote: Thrombolytics dissolve (ie, lyse) the thrombus in a coronary artery

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which cardiomyopathy causes a stiff, hypertrophied left ventricle and risk of sudden death in young athletes?
questions.rationale: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy: asymmetric LVH, outflow obstruction, sudden death; about half inherited.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy (PDF p. 318)
questions.quote: Sudden death common

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Dilated cardiomyopathy is commonly associated with:
questions.rationale: Causes include alcohol abuse and chemotherapy.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Dilated Cardiomyopathy (PDF p. 318)
questions.quote: Alcohol abuse

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Septic, anaphylactic, and neurogenic shock are all types of:
questions.rationale: Distributive shock results from systemic vasodilation.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Shock (PDF p. 318)
questions.quote: Distributive – systemic vasodilation
